newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspected anti-nuclear activists stop German trains.
newsitem.headline: Suspected anti-nuclear activists stop German trains.

text.p: Suspected anti-nuclear activists sabotaged a stretch of high-speed rail track in southern Germany, blocking the line for several hours early on Thursday, police said.
Two freight trains smashed into grappling hooks thrown on to the overhead power cables on the line between Stuttgart and Mannheim, said the border control office in Stuttgart.

The sabotage came a week after a train carrying nuclear waste through eastern France was derailed. The derailment sparked renewed fears about nuclear transportation but officials said there was no radiation leak.

Germany's anti-nuclear activists have focused their efforts in the past few years on stopping nuclear waste shipments -- a campaign that has involved sabotaging railway lines, bomb threats and massive demonstrations.
Last year, more than 19,000 police and border guards were called in to ensure a shipment reached Gorleben medium-term nuclear waste depot near Hanover.
